title: Paloma and the Choir
premise: Ada Brightwater fled her hedge-witch master to disappear into the Ledger Guild, where debts are paid in years, names, and other impossible things. When a prophecy written a century ago surfaces bearing tonight's date and Ada's true name, they learn the guild has been quietly feeding the city's memories to a thing that wears the king's crown—a crown-bound parasite keeping the last dragon's fire alive as its fuel. To survive, Ada must ally with the disgraced royal archivist Sef and the dragon's dying keeper, unbinding the king from his crown before the final gutter of dragon-fire erases every memory in the realm, including their own. In the end Ada chooses to carry the fire themselves, trading their invisibility—and most of their remembered past—for a kingdom that can begin to remember honestly.
about_author: Xanthe Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild ledgers in a coastal trading city before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, memory, and the quiet violence of institutions.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A night of routine ledger-keeping at the Ledger Guild: recording a fisherman's payment of seven years of luck for one safe voyage. Ada takes pride in being nobody, invisible among the ink-stained clerks. Emotional beat: the comfort of anonymity, undercut by a flicker of guilt over what the entries cost people.

chapters.title: Tonight, Written Long Ago
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. While shelving a returned volume, Ada finds a century-old prophecy book whose final entry bears tonight's date—and Ada's birth name, which they buried years ago. The entry ends mid-sentence. Emotional beat: cold dread; the past they fled has found them through paper.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Fell
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Disgraced royal archivist Sef recognizes the prophecy book's seal when Ada comes asking questions in the palace archive's black-market annex. He agrees to help—for a price in guild favors. Emotional beat: wary mutual recognition between two people hiding from institutions.

chapters.title: What the Crown Eats
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Deciphering the prophecy, Sef reveals the 'crown' is a parasite bound to the king a century ago, sustained by harvested memories—memories the guild has been collecting as 'debts.' Emotional beat: horror at realizing Ada's own ledgers fed it.

chapters.title: A Debt Called Ada
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The Guildmaster summons Ada, revealing the guild has known about the prophecy all along and considers Ada its property until the date passes. Ada signs nothing and flees into the rain. Emotional beat: betrayal; invisibility was always someone else's arrangement.

chapters.title: The Keeper of the Last Fire
chapters.summary: Keeper Ysol's POV. In the mountain shrine, ancient keeper Ysol tends the last dragon-fire and feels it guttering. She sends a moth-charm toward the city, seeking whoever the prophecy named. Emotional beat: weary duty and grief for the dragon long dead beneath the flame.

chapters.title: Moths and Messages
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The moth-charm finds Ada in a debtor's flophouse, burning a name into their palm. Following it means leaving the city; staying means the guild. Ada chooses the road. Emotional beat: terrified resolve—the first free choice in years.

chapters.title: Road Through Borrowed Country
chapters.summary: Ada and Sef's alternating POV. On the mountain road, villages have gaps in them: no one remembers the war, the old king, their own dead. Sef teaches Ada archival craft as survival skill. Emotional beat: growing trust; the country itself is forgetting how to grieve.

chapters.title: The Shrine Below the Snowline
chapters.summary: Ysol's POV. Ysol meets the fugitives, tests Ada with a memory-price, and shows them the truth: the fire is the dragon's death still burning, and the crown feeds on everything the fire once illuminated. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by the scale of what must be undone.

chapters.title: Ledger of a Kingdom
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the shrine vault lies the original ledger of the binding—every memory the crown took, indexed by the guild's founders. Ada realizes their own apprenticeship was recruitment into this harvest. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: What My Master Knew
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, flashback-heavy. Ada confronts why they ran from their hedge-witch master: she was a guild collector, and Ada's childhood memories were collateral. The prophecy named Ada because only an unbound memory can read the ledger aloud. Emotional beat: grief finally faced instead of fled.

chapters.title: The Guild Closes Its Books
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Vane's POV. Vane dispatches collectors to retrieve Ada and burn the shrine vault, intending to let the fire die and inherit the crown's power directly. Emotional beat: chilling bureaucratic calm; corruption as accounting.

chapters.title: Collectors on the Stair
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The collectors assault the shrine. Ysol holds the stair with fire-moths while Sef and Ada escape deeper with the ledger. Ysol is taken. Emotional beat: panic, sacrifice, survivor's shame.

chapters.title: Reading Aloud Is Binding
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hidden in the dragon's bone-hollows, Ada learns the unbinding rite: the ledger must be read aloud in the crown's presence by someone whose name appears in it. Every word read returns a memory to the world—but takes one from the reader. Emotional beat: dawning understanding of the price.

chapters.title: Palace of Forgetting
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Using his old credentials, Sef smuggles Ada into the palace during the Feast of Continuity, where the king annually forgets his own coronation. Courtiers orbit the crown like moths. Emotional beat: dread dressed in splendor.

chapters.title: The King Who Isn't There
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada reaches the king and finds a gentle, hollowed man who begs to be told who he is. The crown wakes and offers Ada anything—including their erased past—if they walk away. Emotional beat: temptation rendered intimate and terrible.

chapters.title: Vane's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Vane's POV. Vane arrives with the captured Ysol and the guild's charter, claiming legal right to the crown's inheritance. Sef publicly burns the charter with a stolen coal of dragon-fire. Emotional beat: defiance; institutions are only paper until someone refuses.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Climax begins: Ada reads the ledger aloud as the crown fights back, flooding the hall with false memories. Each line restores something to the kingdom and burns something out of Ada—their master's face, their mother's voice. Emotional beat: sacrificial clarity.

chapters.title: Unbound
chapters.summary: Ysol's POV. Freed mid-reading, Ysol completes the rite's final verse as the crown cracks. The king returns to himself; the thing wearing the crown unravels into a century of stolen names crying out and dispersing. Emotional beat: catharsis and mourning entwined.

chapters.title: Gutter and Kindling
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. With the crown broken, the last dragon-fire begins to die for good. Ada chooses to take the fire into themselves—the price being most of what remains of their remembered life. Emotional beat: quiet, costly triumph; becoming the thing they tended.

chapters.title: Ledgers Closed, Ledgers Opened
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Aftermath: the guild dissolves, debts are struck from the books, and the king establishes an honest archive with Sef at its head. Ada, half-remembering, begins writing down what others recall of them. Emotional beat: bittersweet reconstruction of a self from testimony.

chapters.title: Paloma and the Choir
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue. Years later, Ada keeps a small shrine where the fire now lives gently, and children call the flame paloma—the dove. The kingdom remembers imperfectly but willingly. Ada reads the finished prophecy's last line at last: it was never a warning, only an invitation. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory chosen rather than owed.
